slides.title: Your cleaning checklist keeps failing. It's not you, it's the list.
It's too long
slides.body: A 40-item list tells our brain 'this will take forever'. Keep each list to 5–7 items max.

slides.title: The tasks are too vague
slides.body: 'Clean bathroom' is not a task. 'Wipe the sink' is. If you can't picture doing it, rewrite it.

slides.title: It lives in an app
slides.body: Out of sight, out of mind. Printed lists on the fridge or mirror get used. Notifications get swiped away.

slides.title: It resets by the day, not the week
slides.body: Miss Tuesday and the week feels ruined. Use a list that restarts daily, so every day is a fresh start.

slides.title: No box to tick
slides.body: Checking a box feels good. That little hit is part of what keeps us going. Use it on purpose.

slides.title: A good checklist doesn't judge you. It hands you the next step.
Checklists built for ADHD brains
slides.body: Short, specific, fridge-ready lists are in The Tidy Brain Printable Pack. Link in bio.
